standard_prerequisites.name: Cancellation of a nonzero factor in a domain
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the identity x = fg x into fg = 1, so that the two multipliers are units.

core_obligations: If x and y are associates, write x = uy with u a unit and derive both inclusions of principal ideals, using y = u^{-1}x for the reverse one (proof lines 29592-29593).
Conversely, from (x) = (y) obtain x = fy and y = gx, so x = fg x; since R is a domain this forces fg = 1 and the two elements are associates (proof lines 29593-29596).
proof_roadmap: Translate the two inclusions of principal ideals into mutual divisibility (proof lines 29591-29594).
Cancel the nonzero element x in the identity x = fg x to see that the multipliers are units (proof lines 29594-29596).
difficulty_reason: In a domain the lemma identifies associates with generators of a common principal ideal (statement lines 29585-29589). The proof does not need unique factorization: one direction keeps the unit explicit, and the other direction converts the two inclusions (x) contained in (y) and (y) contained in (x) into the two divisibility relations x = fy and y = gx, substitutes to get x = fg x, and cancels the nonzero element x, which is exactly where the domain hypothesis is used (proof lines 29591-29597). The cancellation step is the one that carries the content, and the author writes both directions out. H2.
